README: THE MONOREPO CONTRACT for FullShot. Filled in from this tool's own manifest.json, publish/manifest.firefox.json, publish/STORE-LISTING.md, publish/package.node.js and a package built from this tree by scripts/pack.mjs — not from the description of it in any planning document. Where the two disagreed, the tree won and the disagreement is recorded in NOTES rather than smoothed over. Every number below was re-measured with the repo's own scripts before it was written down, and the commands that produced it are named next to it. Nothing here changes a single line of FullShot's source: this file is the only required addition. THIS FILE IS NOT A DATED SNAPSHOT — it is corrected in place when the tree moves, and what it used to say is recorded in NOTES.corrections rather than deleted.
name: FullShot
summary: Full-page, visible-area, region and element capture, with an annotation editor, PDF export and on-device redaction.
aiHandoff: The capture leaves the browser as an ai-handoff/1.1 envelope — the image plus the facts a model would otherwise have to guess from pixels: what was captured, at what scale, what was cut, and whether anything was redacted.

storeMetadata._why: TWO BUILDS, THREE STORES. `targets` above is the BUILD axis and it has two entries; this is the STORE axis and it has three. The chromium zip goes to Chrome AND Edge byte-identical, so `target` below is what makes that sharing a DECLARATION rather than an accident — two rows naming one target cannot drift into two builds. Every listing field that differs per store lives under `dir`; everything all three accept lives under `sharedDir`.
storeMetadata._servedWhy: `served` is a GATE, not membership. A row exists for a store that is deferred so its facts are recorded once instead of rediscovered at submission. A missing directory PRINTS while unserved and FAILS once served — which is how owner-gated work (accounts, screenshots) avoids turning CI permanently red. Nothing is served today: FullShot has never been submitted anywhere.
storeMetadata._vocabularyWhy: The store ids are NOT declared here. They are derived from scripts/schema/tool.schema.json -> properties.listings.properties, which check-catalog.mjs already treats as the store vocabulary. A fourth list of store names would be the second declaration and the first to drift; check-store-metadata.mjs asserts this block, `targets.*.stores` and `listings` all agree.
storeMetadata._limitsWhy: A LIMIT WITH NO `source` IS REFUSED, NOT ENFORCED. check-store-metadata.mjs fails the build on any `max` that arrives without a URL and a fetch date, because an invented limit fires on CORRECT input — this factory has already rejected its own fixture at 129 characters against a made-up '120 or fewer'. Everything below was read from the store's own documentation on 2026-08-20; everything that could NOT be is in `_unverified` and is deliberately unenforced.
_unverified: EDGE NAME LIMIT (45) and AMO NAME LIMIT (50) — MDN states both, dated 'as of February 2024', but learn.microsoft.com states no name limit anywhere and extensionworkshop states none either. MDN is a secondary source for another vendor's rule. NOT enforced until re-fetched from the store itself.

CHROME LONG-DESCRIPTION MAXIMUM — the widely-repeated 16,000 appears NOWHERE on developer.chrome.com. cws-dashboard-listing, best-listing, prepare and program-policies all describe the field with no number. NOT enforced.
PERMANENCE OF THE CHROME ITEM ID AND EDGE PRODUCT ID — neither store states in writing that its assigned id is immutable. Assume it is; do not write it down as sourced fact.
AMO SCREENSHOT COUNT AND DIMENSION LIMITS — the docs say 'no practical limit' and give recommendations, not requirements.

title.txt.source: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/name (fetched 2026-08-20) — verbatim: "short, plain text string (maximum of 75 characters)"

edge._patchWhy: Microsoft documents exactly two required edits to a Chrome package: remove `update_url`, and rebrand if the name or description says 'Chrome'. FullShot's manifest carries no update_url and its name is __MSG_appName__ — measured 2026-08-20 — so no patch is needed TODAY. The key is present and null so that the day one is needed it is a value, not a new mechanism.

short-description.txt.source: https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/create-an-appealing-listing/ (fetched 2026-08-20) — verbatim: "The summary description for your add-on is limited to 250 characters"

permissions.activeTab: Captures only the tab the user acted on, from the moment they click the toolbar button or press a capture shortcut — the least-privileged way to read the current page, and it grants no standing access to any site.
permissions.scripting: Injects the capture engine into the active tab on demand, so it can measure the page, scroll it to load and stitch the full length, and let the user pick a region or an element — instead of declaring a persistent content script on every page.
permissions.downloads: Saves a finished screenshot (PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF) or an exported GIF/WebM when the user chooses to save it. FullShot starts no download on its own.
permissions.storage: Keeps the user's own preferences — image format, capture options, filename template, PDF options, theme — in chrome.storage.sync. No page content and no screenshots are put there.
permissions.unlimitedStorage: Finished screenshots are kept in a local IndexedDB history so they can be reopened, edited and exported later. Screenshots are large; without this the default quota silently drops the user's own capture history. The data never leaves the device.

optionalHostPermissions.<all_urls>: OPTIONAL and requested at run time, never at install: only when the user turns on expanding scrollable content inside cross-origin iframes, or Batch URL capture. Decline it and every other feature keeps working — single-tab capture needs activeTab alone.

absent.vendor/core/: No shared core is vendored. The reason has changed since this file was first drafted and the old one is now false: scripts/sync-core.mjs EXISTS, and core/v1 holds settings.js, storage.js and jobs.js. What has not happened is a sync against this tree — there is no vendor/core/ and no .coremeta.json — so "core" stays null and vendor/core/ stays out of package.include. `node scripts/check-core-sync.mjs fullshot` passes today for that reason and says so: "this tool vendors no core — tool.json declares no core channel and there is no vendor/core/ directory — consistent". When it lands the directory is vendor/core/ — NEVER _core/, which Chrome refuses to load.
absent.content_security_policy: manifest.json declares none. Not a defect and not a false claim — the zero-network claim is true and measured — but it is the difference between a promise a scanner checks and a rule the browser enforces. scripts/policy-check.mjs warns about it by name: extension_pages with connect-src 'none' makes a fetch() from an extension page fail at runtime even if one is ever added. The template's own manifest already carries that header, so adopting it is a copy rather than a design.

NOTES.$schema: Added the day scripts/schema/tool.schema.json actually existed. It drives editor autocomplete and hover docs only; the gate is scripts/lib/toolinfo.mjs, because the checks that matter are cross-file (does the manifest exist, does every listed test path resolve, does surface match the category directory) and no JSON Schema can express them. The three non-schema keys below — README, absent, NOTES — load fine but are reported by the loader as unknown keys with "nothing reads it", which is accurate and is the point: they are for the human reading the file, not for a script.
NOTES.status: "wip", not "shipping". "shipping" means listed in a store. FullShot v1.10.2 is built, packaged for both engines and green on every simulation, and it has no listing anywhere — see listings, all null. Flip this the day the first store URL exists, not the day the zip does.
NOTES.summary: This field is the catalogue line, not the manifest description. The description USED to be over the store's limit and that is now fixed: `node scripts/policy-check.mjs fullshot` re-run 2026-08-22 reports PASS "name/short_name/description within store limits — checked across all 55 locale(s)". CHANGELOG [1.10.2] records the fix (en appDescription 137 -> 111 characters, longest catalogue now 132, longest locale name 44). What this entry said before, so the correction is legible rather than silent: "the en description ... is 137 characters against a 132 cap ... 40 of the 55 catalogues exceed 132, the longest at 199, and three locale NAMES (ca, es, es_419) exceed the 45-character name cap ... it is the single thing standing between this tree and a submission." That was true when written and is false now; nothing about store metadata length blocks a submission today.
NOTES.aiHandoff: AI-HANDOFF-ENVELOPE.md declares ai-handoff/1.1 normative for FullShot 1.11+, implemented in pages/common.js (fsAi*) and consumed by pages/result.js, graded by test/aihandoff-sim.node.js. The manifest version is 1.10.2 — so this line describes the tree, which is what this file describes, and not necessarily the bytes of any built zip.
NOTES.core: null on purpose. scripts/sync-core.mjs exists now, so the remaining condition is a run, not a script: vendor a core only once sync-core has been run against this tree and there is a vendor/core/.coremeta.json of hashes for check-core-sync to verify. Declaring { channel: v1 } before that asserts a relationship nothing verifies, against a directory that is not there.
NOTES.package: VERIFIED TWICE, AGAINST A BUILT ARTIFACT AND AGAINST THE REPO'S OWN LOADER. `node scripts/pack.mjs fullshot --target firefox --out <scratch> --release` (re-run 2026-08-22, EXIT 0) selects 85 files — 55 locale catalogues plus 30 code/assets — and the archive reads back as 85 entries: background.js and manifest.json at the root, and _locales/ content/ icons/ pages/ popup/ below it. scripts/policy-check.mjs, applying the include/exclude rules above through scripts/lib/toolinfo.mjs packagedFiles(), reports the same 85 with zero locales reachable only by the unconditional locale collector — i.e. this block and the built zip name the same file set, not merely the same count. NOTE ON PROVENANCE: this entry used to cite "the shipped publish/fullshot-1.10.1.zip". No zip is present in publish/ today — all twelve were deleted 2026-08-20, see publish/STALE-FIREFOX-ARTIFACTS-2026-08-20.md — and `node scripts/check-store-packages.mjs fullshot`, run bare on this clean checkout, says so in as many words: "ZERO PACKAGES WERE PRESENT, so this run proved nothing about any artifact." (Conditional on the subject being absent — it searches publish/ and dist/, so after a local build it grades what it finds.) The list that produced a zip is ALLOW in publish/package.node.js; scripts/pack.mjs is what ci.yml and release.yml actually invoke.
NOTES.package.LICENSE: DELIBERATELY RECORDED, NOT COPIED FROM THE TEMPLATE: LICENSE is absent from FullShot's allowlist and absent from the shipped zip (checked by reading the archive's central directory), while the template allowlists it explicitly because PolyForm Shield's notice is required to travel with every copy. FullShot's root LICENSE is PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 as well. Adding it to the package is a licence question for the owner, so it is named here rather than silently added to include.
NOTES.package.exclude: Two entries name paths that do not exist in THIS TOOL'S tree today — .claude/** and dist/**. (These globs are tool-relative, which is the reading that matters: .claude/ does exist at the REPOSITORY root, and dist/ appears there whenever anyone builds. Neither is under Extension/Full_Screen_Shot/, so neither is packaged, and neither exclude has ever had anything to fire on.) They are kept deliberately: both are directories that appear without anyone deciding to add them (an agent's config, a build output), and an exclude that fires zero times costs nothing while an exclude added after the fact costs a leaked package. Reference/** and i18n/** and test/** do exist and do fire.
NOTES.targets.firefox: The Firefox package is built by applying publish/manifest.firefox.json to manifest.json AS AN RFC 7386 MERGE PATCH — converted 2026-08-18. The overlay is 511 bytes and carries five keys (background, browser_specific_settings, options_ui, minimum_chrome_version, options_page); it does NOT restate version, description or the permissions, so a bump can no longer be right-in-one-file-and-wrong-in-the-other. `node scripts/check-version.mjs fullshot` grades exactly that and PASSES: "publish/manifest.firefox.json is an overlay — it does not restate the version, so it cannot drift from it." In the MERGED manifest the packaged add-on carries BOTH background forms — service_worker and scripts [pages/db.js, pages/batch.js, background.js] — plus options_ui alongside options_page, which is correct: each engine reads its own key. WHAT THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY, corrected 2026-08-22: "built by swapping in publish/manifest.firefox.json wholesale ... kept equal to manifest.json by hand ... which is why a bump has to be right twice", and it read the facts back out of publish/fullshot-1.10.1-firefox.zip, which no longer exists.
NOTES.targets.firefox.geckoId: SETTLED AND PERMANENT — the owner action that stood here is DONE. browser_specific_settings.gecko.id = "fullshot@nikatru.com", derived from publish/identity.json (slug + ownerDomain, domain chosen 2026-08-18). Three independent graders agree, all re-run 2026-08-22: scripts/policy-check.mjs PASSES "the Firefox add-on id is set — fullshot@nikatru.com -- and agrees with publish/identity.json"; publish/verify-firefox-package.node.js PASSES "gecko.id is NOT the placeholder", the Mozilla email-format limb and the 80-character limb (20); and scripts/pack.mjs prints the id while writing the package. WHAT THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY, and it was true when written: "🔴 OWNER ACTION, AND IT IS PERMANENT ... carries gecko.id = fullshot@REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-DOMAIN.example ... nobody but the owner can pick the replacement." The permanence warning still stands as a fact about AMO — it fixes the identity at first signing — it just no longer describes an open item.
NOTES.tests: All eleven were re-run individually on Node v24.18.0 on 2026-08-22 — ten test/*.node.js sims plus test/pixel-sim/run.js — and every one EXITED 0, each exit code captured on its own line rather than inferred from a loop. test/e2e/ is deliberately not listed: it needs a real Chromium and a Playwright install, so it belongs to the gated browser tier rather than to the per-push one. A listed path that stops resolving does not fail, it silently stops running, which is why the array is exact paths rather than a glob.
NOTES.policy.permissions: Sourced from publish/STORE-LISTING.md §4, which is what the store dashboard receives, and cross-checked against the five permissions manifest.json actually declares. `node scripts/policy-check.mjs fullshot` now grades that agreement directly and reports "5 permission(s), all justified — activeTab, scripting, downloads, storage, unlimitedStorage", plus "no static host_permissions" for the optional <all_urls>. Keeping the two texts in one voice is the point: the justification a reviewer reads and the justification the repo asserts should not be two separately-maintained documents.
NOTES.policy.networkAllowlist: EMPTY, AND MEASURED TWICE. A scan of the packaged file set for fetch( · XMLHttpRequest · WebSocket · EventSource · sendBeacon returns nothing, with a control pattern over the same files matching to prove the scan was looking; scripts/policy-check.mjs repeats it on the packaged set with comments and string literals blanked first, and reports "zero network calls in 15 packaged script(s) — allowlist is empty, as claimed". The blanking matters: grep the raw source and you grade the comment in background.js that says there are no network calls. FullShot collects no analytics and contacts no server — including the redaction detector, which runs entirely on the device.
NOTES.gate status today: GREEN, RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22, exit codes captured one per line: `node scripts/policy-check.mjs fullshot` EXIT 0 (15 passed) · `node scripts/check-version.mjs fullshot` EXIT 0 (3 passed) · `node scripts/check-core-sync.mjs fullshot` EXIT 0 · `node scripts/check-store-metadata.mjs fullshot` EXIT 0 (25 passed · 1 owner action(s)) — the summary line prints BOTH halves and both are recorded here on purpose: the owner action is the empty store/_shared/screenshots/, and an exit code of 0 beside a bare pass-count hides work that is owed. This entry used to record only "25 passed" · `node scripts/pack.mjs fullshot --target firefox --release` EXIT 0 · `node Extension/Full_Screen_Shot/publish/verify-firefox-package.node.js` EXIT 0 both bare and with --zip on that freshly built package. `node scripts/check-store-packages.mjs fullshot` EXIT 0 but grades NOTHING ON A CLEAN CHECKOUT — read its printed line, not its code: no zip is present in publish/ to open. THE PRECONDITION IS PART OF THE CLAIM: the script's DEFAULT_DIRS are ['publish','dist'], so on a machine that has just built it opens and grades what it finds, and ci.yml's `package` job calls it with `--dir dist` on the zip it built four steps earlier. What is durable is the SHAPE — bare, with the subject absent, this gate proves nothing about any artifact — not the sentence an empty tree makes it print. THIS ENTRY USED TO READ, and was true when written: "policy-check ... exits 1 — 11 passed, 1 FAILED ... check-version ... exits 1 on the missing CHANGELOG.md." Both failures are closed — CHANGELOG.md exists with top entry [1.10.2] and the locale length overruns came down in 1.10.2. WARNINGS ARE NOT FAILURES AND THE COUNT IS MOVING, so read the run rather than a number here: the standing one is no CSP connect-src to back the zero-network claim (see absent.content_security_policy). A second, "8 locale(s) are missing keys the default has", was printing over 9 CLDR plural-form keys per locale that fall back to en; it is being closed in policy-check.mjs itself as a false positive, so the same command can honestly print 1 or 2 warnings depending on merge order. EXIT 0 is the stable fact.
NOTES.listings: All null: nothing is listed yet. When they land, remember that the metadata cannot be shared with a sibling tool — Microsoft certification 10.1.4 requires each listing to carry its own — and that a Chrome Web Store publisher account holds at most 20 extensions, enforced per publisher, which is a limit on the account rather than on any tool in it. The privacy policy is served from nikatru.com; publish/PRIVACY-POLICY.html is the source of that page, not the published copy. The URL is settled and live: publish/identity.json carries https://nikatru.com/fullshot/privacy, filled 2026-08-21, and a GET on 2026-08-22 answered 200 with zero redirect hops. store/_shared/privacy-policy-url.txt is the copy a human pastes into the three dashboards; it is tracked and corrected separately from this file.

NOTES.LICENSE Required Notice: RECORDED HERE ONLY SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT EDIT THE WRONG LINE, because two records in publish/ point at it. `grep -n 'Required Notice' Extension/Full_Screen_Shot/LICENSE` returns FIVE lines — :35, :38, :168, :173, :180 — and FOUR of the five must not be touched. :35 and :38 sit ABOVE the rule at :166, inside PolyForm Shield 1.0.0's own §Notices worked example — :38 is the "Copyright Yoyodyne, Inc. (http://example.com)" example — and :172-173 of the same file says the text above the rule is the licence verbatim and unmodified, do not edit it. :173 is the second half of that very sentence ("...do not edit it. The Required Notice line is the one thing this"), so it MATCHES THE GREP AND IS ITSELF PROSE INSIDE THE WARNING — a fifth non-editable line, not a candidate. :180 is this repo's explanatory echo of that same example. THE ONE FILLABLE SLOT IS LINE 168: "Required Notice: Copyright <OWNER LEGAL NAME OR COMPANY> (<OPTIONAL URL>)", flagged at :170 with ">>> OWNER ACTION — replace the line above BEFORE the first commit. <<<". Editing a licence grant is an owner act; nothing in this repo may write that line. WHAT THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY, and it was an undercount when written: "has FOUR lines matching 'Required Notice'", enumerating :35, :38, :180 and the slot at :168 and omitting :173 — which the same entry then cited as prose two clauses later, so the line was read and not counted. A reader invited to run the grep got five hits with one unaccounted for, in the one document whose whole job is stopping an edit to the wrong licence line. Counted 2026-08-22 with the grep named above, by reading the file, not by reading a note about it; LICENSE was opened READ-ONLY and is unchanged.
